ambiguity_resolutions.basis: The current hypothesis says elliptic addition signature but does not define a finite local tensor; a canonical sign tensor makes every identity and source witness replayable.
ambiguity_resolutions.question: What exact tensor is transformed?
ambiguity_resolutions.resolution: Freeze one complete arity-four Boolean tensor whose bits select the signs of four public x-coordinate lifts and whose entry records the exact elliptic sum constraint, including identity and exceptional cases.

ambiguity_resolutions.basis: A shared holographic basis is the strongest reusable interpretation consistent with the hypothesis and prevents per-instance orbit fitting from becoming uncharged advice.
ambiguity_resolutions.question: Which basis freedom is permitted?
ambiguity_resolutions.resolution: Use one invertible public 2x2 matrix shared by all four legs and frozen independently of the target; independent per-leg or target-selected matrices are excluded from this gate.

critical_experiments.negative_decision: Reject the shared-basis transform before scaling if the generic parity and Grassmann-Pluecker equations are inconsistent or only target-selected bases work.
critical_experiments.next_action: Derive one canonical four-sign elliptic addition tensor and solve the target-independent shared-2x2-basis matchgate equations on symbolic and tiny fixtures; do not execute the review-required 360-CPU-hour campaign.
critical_experiments.positive_decision: Approve only a tiny exact identity preflight after the canonical Boolean signature, shared basis grammar, parity equations, Grassmann-Pluecker convention, and source semantics are machine-checkable.
critical_experiments.title: Spinor-matchgate addition transform
critical_experiments.uncertainty: Does one public target-independent shared binary basis map a complete arity-four elliptic addition signature into the matchgate variety, with exact source-preserving self-reduction?
